title: RIROS: A Parallel RTL Fault SImulation FRamework with TwO-Dimensional Parallelism and Unified Schedule
problem: RTL fault simulation for safety-critical applications is time-consuming due to imbalanced task loads from dynamic fault propagation paths, slowing verification cycles.
method: The system combines two forms of parallelism: dividing work across both the circuit's structural layout (structural-level parallelism) and across the different faults being tested (fault-level parallelism). When a processor finishes early, it steals remaining work from busier processors through work-stealing, keeping all processors busy. A unified schedule handles both computation tasks and synchronization points between processors in a single plan, eliminating idle gaps where processors would otherwise wait.
key_novelty: First RTL fault simulation framework using two-dimensional parallelism (structural-level and fault-level) to balance uneven task loads.
contributions: Work-stealing mechanism for handling numerous low-load tasks
Unified scheduling approach eliminating synchronization bubbles
primary_theme: Parallel RTL fault simulation for safety-critical chips
